correctness.rationale: The displayed chromatic-number formulas themselves are correct. I independently brute-forced all 111 dual/outer/total cases for complete-multipartite profiles through order seven with no mismatch. The universal proof follows from the same-part criterion: two vertices in one part are \(M\)-visible exactly when the complement of \(M\) contains a vertex in a different part. However, the submitted RESULT contains a genuine proof error in its total-coloring paragraph for \(r\ge3\): the proposed partition \(V_1, V\setminus V_1\) is not always total (for example, in \(K_{2,1,1}\), the class \(V\setminus V_1\) blocks every geodesic between the two vertices of \(V_1\)). A correct two-color proof instead splits two non-singleton parts, or, when only one part is non-singleton, splits it and assigns singleton parts to both colors. Thus the theorem is true even though this record's written proof is defective.
risks: Because the record is scientifically rejected for prior coverage, no proof repair is proposed as a publication repair.
